key_insight: A systematic empirical comparison shows that practical utility of vision–language–action (VLA) models for generalist robots depends less on raw size and more on multimodal alignment, grounded action representations, and diverse, task‑balanced training data.
problem_solved: Clarifies which architectural choices, data composition and training practices actually improve real-world robot performance when combining vision, language and action — resolving confusion about what matters most for building generalist robotic agents.
method: Benchmark and compare multiple VLA model variants across standardized robot task suites to measure real-world effectiveness.
Ablation studies isolating components (perception backbone, language grounding, action decoder/representation) to quantify their contributions.
Analysis of training data diversity and transfer behavior, yielding practical guidelines for model design and deployment.
impact: Provides actionable guidance for researchers and engineers on where to invest effort (alignment, grounded action outputs, and diverse task data) to build more robust, transferable VLA models for robots, accelerating progress toward generalist robotic systems.
visual_elements: Architecture pipeline diagram showing vision encoder → language encoder → action decoder and where key design choices apply
Bar/line charts from ablations highlighting performance impact of perception, language grounding and action representation choices
Matrix/table comparing model variants against task categories (manipulation, navigation, language-conditioned tasks) to show strengths/weaknesses
Dataset/task composition heatmap or pie chart illustrating the importance of task diversity in training
paper_title: What matters in building vision–language–action models for generalist robots
paper_authors: Xinghang Li, Peiyan Li, Long Qian, Minghuan Liu, Dong Wang
